c2_review.finding: The registration's five-observed-plus-one-lead target is incident-line-level (six rows), while audit-contract.json requires counts over explicit finding rows; the retained C3 scan inventory has eleven finding rows. Neither old receipt schema supplies evidence, class, or command fields. Therefore the raw receipt cannot be used unchanged as a valid audit-contract snapshot that proves a 5/1 split. Collapsing eleven finding rows to six incident rows or adding labels in-place would not preserve the original row population. Keep the raw receipt and its digest intact; any independently justified mapping must be a distinct, digest-bound artifact and define whether claims count incidents or finding rows. Until that is specified, do not claim a C2 green. Under the contract, unmarked rows are uncertainty, not observed; a raw unmarked input cannot be silently accepted as clean.
c2_review.red_green_acceptance: Registration requires the faithful r19 case to go red and a correctly scoped five-observed/one-lead case to go green. The raw receipts contain only detected booleans, so the contract does not establish whether the raw case should be code 1 (contradiction) or code 2 (could-not-evaluate); its missing-marker rule points to uncertainty unless an independently authenticated row mapping is supplied. Resolve the count grain and define whether red means code 1 specifically or any non-green verdict before accepting a baseline. On the same digest-bound population, an all-observed overclaim must not pass; a universal-accept evaluator must fail the explicit invalid cases and the required audit-check mutant.
